questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Testing output shapes” in this lesson?
options: This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Write down the expected axes and element count, then assert the observed shape. For layout-related topics, also check contiguity and whether storage is shared.
questions.answer_key: Write down the expected axes and element count, then assert the observed shape. For layout-related topics, also check contiguity and whether storage is shared.
questions.explanation: Testing output shapes: Write down the expected axes and element count, then assert the observed shape. For layout-related topics, also check contiguity and whether storage is shared.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Testing gradients”, what should a learner verify?
options: Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
include positive and negative cases, appropriate tolerances, gradient/shape assertions, and a documented artifact-trust policy.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
questions.answer_key: include positive and negative cases, appropriate tolerances, gradient/shape assertions, and a documented artifact-trust policy.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: include positive and negative cases, appropriate tolerances, gradient/shape assertions, and a documented artifact-trust policy.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Testing custom layers”?
options: Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not hide all exceptions or assume bitwise equality across devices and package versions.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
questions.answer_key: Do not hide all exceptions or assume bitwise equality across devices and package versions.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not hide all exceptions or assume bitwise equality across devices and package versions.
